chapter: Russell's band, records and Armstrong in the studio
title: Clarinet on 'Slow and Steady' and hating the clarinet
summary: The Brunswick session of November 14, 1928 under Oliver's name was Holmes's first record; he says he hated clarinet but all saxophonists had to play it.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: And on November 14, 1928, according to the Brunswick ledgers, you were in the studio. It was issued under Oliver's name. And it was a tune by Oliver, and it was
And you recognized yourself playing clarinet on that.
And Higgenbotham was in the band. Who was it? Metcalf on trumpet...
Probably Teddy Hill. Could have been. I don't know... That's about the first Hill I can remember.
Right. And at that point, you had some comments to say about playing clarinet.
You might say just a little...
Well, I'm not a clarinet player. I'm not going to advertise the clarinet!
No. You might say that you really didn't like to play clarinet.
I hated to play it. They were fightin' words to me when they said, "Play the clarinet."
But in those days it was expected that a saxophonist...

All saxophonists were supposed to have a clarinet. And when you have it, you're supposed to play it. I hated it. But I had to have one, because all the parts of the music were made for clarinet and saxophone.
So here was your first recording and here was this part
Oh yeah. I did the best I could with what I had. I didn't like it. No wonder I didn't hear that record.
